articles.title: 5 Advanced Walter MCP Prompts for Power Users
articles.excerpt: Most people using Walter Writes AI's MCP server never get past the basic version: paste a paragraph, ask Claude to humanize it, done. That works, but it leaves most of the integration unused. Once Wal…
articles.body: Most people using Walter Writes AI's MCP server never get past the basic version: paste a paragraph, ask Claude to humanize it, done. That works, but it leaves most of the integration unused. Once Walter is connected as an MCP server, Claude has three tools it can call, and it can call them in sequence, conditionally, and across many inputs. In Claude Code, it can also read the drafts from your repo and write the results back. That turns a one-off paraphrase into something closer to a content pipeline: detect first, humanize only what needs it, lock the terms that must survive, and report per file. This post covers the setup in two minutes, then five prompts that use it properly. Each prompt is in a code block so you can copy it straight into Claude or Claude Code.

You pick a denied claim, it reads the synthetic chart + payer policy, and it returns a verdict, quote-backed evidence, an editable letter, and peer-to-peer talking points. The model is optional. articles.title: Zoom your landing page to 200% before you ship it: a two-minute check
articles.excerpt: Most of us check a landing page at the size of our own screen. Plenty of visitors don't see it that way: they zoom in, use a larger default font, or browse on a small window. Here is a short check tha…
articles.body: Most of us check a landing page at the size of our own screen. Plenty of visitors don't see it that way: they zoom in, use a larger default font, or browse on a small window. Here is a short check that catches the most common breakage. The check Open the page in a desktop browser. Press Ctrl and + (Cmd and + on a Mac) until you reach 200%. Scroll the whole page, top to bottom. Zoom further, to 400%, and scroll again. WCAG asks for text that can be resized to 200% without losing content or function (success criterion 1.4.4), and for content that reflows into a single column at a 320 CSS pixel width, which is what 400% zoom gives you on a 1280 pixel wide window (1.4.10), without needing to scroll sideways to read a line. What usually breaks Fixed-height hero sections.

articles.title: Your SKIP LOCKED Queue Can Run a Job Twice. Heartbeats and Fencing Tokens Make It Safe
articles.excerpt: Book: Event-Driven Architecture Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for d…
articles.body: Book: Event-Driven Architecture Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub Say your receipt job renders a PDF and emails it. It usually takes 20 seconds, and the worker's lease on the job is 30. Then one morning the PDF service is slow, the job takes 45 seconds, and a customer gets two receipts. Nothing crashed and nothing was logged: two workers ran the same job at once, each doing exactly what its code said. This is a classic way for a Postgres -backed job queue to misbehave. Postgres is doing what you asked: a lease expired while the work was still running.

articles.title: My git changelog generator learned that merge commits hide the truth — parents are a graph, not a line
articles.excerpt: I built a git changelog generator that diffs two commits and emits structured release notes. First version walked git log A..B and treated every commit as a straight line. Clean, deterministic, wrong.…
articles.body: I built a git changelog generator that diffs two commits and emits structured release notes. First version walked git log A..B and treated every commit as a straight line. Clean, deterministic, wrong. The bug: on a repo with a normal PR workflow, git log A..B on the main branch shows merge commits but NOT the individual feature commits they brought in. My changelog would say "Merge pull request #42" and nothing else. Humans reading the release notes got zero signal about what actually shipped. The fix wasn't a bigger diff. It was changing what I walk. I switched to git log --first-parent A..B for the branch-level summary, then for each merge commit, git log ^parent1 parent2 to enumerate the commits that merge actually introduced.

articles.title: Supply Chain Consequences of a MOVEit Authentication Bypass
articles.excerpt: Supply Chain Consequences of a MOVEit Authentication Bypass The interesting property of CVE-2026-89068 is not the CVSS score. It is that the vulnerability lives on a platform whose purpose is to conne…
articles.body: Supply Chain Consequences of a MOVEit Authentication Bypass The interesting property of CVE-2026-89068 is not the CVSS score. It is that the vulnerability lives on a platform whose purpose is to connect organisations to each other, which means a flaw in it becomes a question for every relationship the platform supports. The flaw A missing critical step in authentication in the LDAP module of Progress MOVEit Transfer, classed as CWE-304 and scored CVSS v3.1 8.1 with a remote, unauthenticated vector. Affected builds are before 2025.1.6 and 2026.0.0 through 2026.0.3. Fixed builds are 2025.1.6 and 2026.0.4. No exploitation was confirmed at publication. Why the blast radius extends past the patched node Managed file transfer platforms hold standing credentials for external parties.

articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.title: 'Lanterns' shocking finale left us with a lot of unanswered questions for a potential season 2
articles.excerpt: John Stewart goes rogue in Sector 2814 and embraces fear hopefully leading into season 2
articles.body: HBO and HBO Max's " Lanterns " served up its big cliffhanger finale on Oct. 4, 2026, and we’ve been slowly digesting thoughts on what the creative direction and ultimate legacy of this debut season were. While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling. After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return.

articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
